medical_justification: A lesion keeps its diagnosis when framed slightly tighter or looser; scale is capped at 0.8 so the lesion border - a key diagnostic feature - stays in frame.
Skin lesions have no canonical left-right orientation; a mirrored mole is the same mole.
Dermoscopy has no fixed 'up'; the camera angle is arbitrary.
Rotation is a pure camera-orientation change. Asymmetry (the 'A' of ABCDE) is rotation-invariant, so it is preserved.
Mimics real illumination and exposure variation between clinics. Kept small - see A3.5: beyond ~0.3 the shift exceeds the real Benign/Malignant brightness gap.
Absorbs white-balance differences only. Capped at 0.02 (~7 degrees) because pigment colour is diagnostic signal; larger values recolour the lesion itself.
An affine rescale of intensities, identical in train and eval; carries no label information.
